description: MULTI-SOLID STEP IMPORT GOLDEN (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-4b): a STEP file carrying TWO disjoint solids imports as ONE multi-lump body (a lump-sorted Compound), NOT as N bodies and NOT as a rejection. `data` in model.json is the byte-deterministic STEP export of a Compound of two 20x20x20 cubes — cube A at x in [0,20], cube B at x in [30,50], a 10 mm gap — authored B-BEFORE-A so the STEP's solid order is the REVERSE of the deterministic lump sort; the `import` BASE feature parses it and lumps.assemble_lumps re-orders the lumps (centroid x/y/z, then volume) so the imported body is byte-identical regardless of OCCT's reader order. Locks the MB-4b import path end to end: multi-solid STEPControl_Reader transfer -> per-solid lump extraction -> explicit lump sort -> ONE Compound body -> analytic compound roll-up -> tessellation -> content-addressed GLB. The same body reads shells=2 (two lumps) and rolls up the SAME analytic 16000 mm^3 / 4800 mm^2 as the MB-0 multibody-two-disjoint-boxes golden, but produced HERE by a single import feature (one Bodies-panel row) rather than two extrudes. Through the shared golden runner this also proves import byte-determinism in-process AND across an interpreter restart, and the parametrized STEP round-trip re-exports the multi-lump body as a multi-solid AP214 file and re-imports it losslessly.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Cube A: an axis-aligned 20x20x20 box spanning x,y,z in [0,20]. Cube B: the same box translated +30 in x, spanning x in [30,50], y,z in [0,20]. The 10 mm gap in x (A ends at x=20, B starts at x=30) makes the two solids DISJOINT — they share no face, edge, or vertex — so STEP import preserves them as two separate lumps of one Compound body (import is not a boolean; solids are kept AS AUTHORED, never fused).

volume = A + B = 20*20*20 + 20*20*20 = 8000 + 8000 = 16000 mm^3 exactly. Disjoint lumps, so the compound roll-up (Sigma volume over the body's solids) is exact with no overlap subtraction. Measured deviation vs analytic: ~7e-12 mm^3 (a few ulp at the 1.6e4 scale, from two GProp integrations summed in float64 plus the STEP transfer).
surface_area = 2 lumps * 6 faces * (20*20 = 400) = 2 * 2400 = 4800 mm^2. Every face of both lumps is external (nothing is fused), so all 12 faces contribute. Measured deviation: ~1e-13 mm^2.

centroid = (25, 10, 10) mm: lump A (V=8000, centroid (10,10,10)) and lump B (V=8000, centroid (40,10,10)) give x = (8000*10 + 8000*40)/16000 = 25.0; y = 10 and z = 10 by symmetry (both lumps span y,z in [0,20]). Volume-weighted, computed analytically over the body's solids, never re-meshed. Measured deviation: <= 1e-14 mm on every component.

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[50,20,20]: the union of A's AABB [0,0,0]..[20,20,20] and B's AABB [30,0,0]..[50,20,20]. STEP carries world coordinates unchanged and the union of two axis-aligned boxes is exact, so all six bounds are EXACT (measured deviation 0.0).

topology (summed over the body's lumps): each cube has 6 faces, 12 edges, 1 closed shell -> 12 faces, 24 edges, 2 SHELLS. shells=2 is the load-bearing multi-lump assertion: the imported body is genuinely two lumps, so the shell count is 2, not 1. Per-lump Euler-Poincare cross-check: V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 2, a valid closed manifold solid; the body is two such shells.

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, faceted per-face normals, no vertex sharing across faces — the box-golden convention): each cube face is a planar quad -> 4 vertices / 2 triangles; 6 faces per lump = 24 vertices / 12 triangles; two lumps = 48 vertices / 24 triangles.

DETERMINISM PROOF: the STEP `data` authors cube B before cube A, so the reader's solid order does NOT match the lump sort; lumps.assemble_lumps imposes the (centroid x, y, z, volume) order, placing A (x-centroid 10) before B (x-centroid 40). The imported Compound is therefore byte-identical across in-process rebuilds AND a fresh interpreter (the runner's three determinism legs), independent of OCCT's traversal order — the one new §MB-4 determinism knob, exercised here.

MEASURED 2026-07-19 (build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9) through the real evaluate_tree import path: volume 15999.9999999999927, area 4799.9999999999991, centroid (25.0,10.0,10.0), bbox exact, topology 12/24/2, mesh 48/24. GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned (brittle across glTF-writer upgrades); the runner asserts it internally consistent and byte-deterministic in-process and across an interpreter restart.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). This is TWO disjoint planar B-reps round-tripped through STEP and composed ANALYTICALLY (combine_properties: Sigma volume, volume-weighted centroid, unioned AABB) — no boolean, no AABB padding. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-19, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9): volume ~7e-12 mm^3, surface_area ~1e-13 mm^2, bounding_box exactly 0.0 on all six bounds, centroid <= 1e-14 mm. Documented ceiling 1e-9 is ~140x the observed worst case (~7e-12, volume — two GProp integrations summed through the STEP transfer), headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). Same tolerance and rationale as the MB-0 multibody-two-disjoint-boxes golden (same analytic geometry, reached by import instead of two extrudes). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
